name: Green (Sirun) Wang
bio: I am an undergraduate at UC Berkeley studying political economy and applied mathematics. I am interested in how institutions and information shape what people value and believe, particularly how preferences and beliefs develop together in different institutional settings.

training.summary: My coursework includes quantitative microeconomics, probability, and mathematics, alongside political economy, world history, and Chinese literary history. This fall, I am taking courses in formal models of political science and the economic institutions of capitalism, with course papers planned in both.

inProgress.title: The Economic Institutions of Capitalism in Historical Perspective

exploratoryQuestion.title: Monetary valuation and preferences
exploratoryQuestion.status: Exploratory interest; not a finding or a confirmed course-paper topic
exploratoryQuestion.question: Can expressing different forms of value in monetary terms change what people come to value?
exploratoryQuestion.note: I would like to explore this question in the context of capitalist institutions. The relationship between monetary valuation and preference formation is a starting point for further study.
